headline: CISA adds actively exploited Drupal core RCE flaw "Fail2Install" (CVE-2026-132165) to KEV
summary: CISA has added CVE-2026-132165, a critical remote code execution flaw in Drupal core known as Fail2Install (CVSS 9.8), to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. US federal agencies must patch it by November 27, 2026. Exploit details have also been published.

headline: North Korea-linked PolinRider campaign plants Python loader in over 7,600 GitHub repositories
summary: SafeDep reports that the PolinRider campaign has hidden a Python loader in thousands of GitHub repositories, inside small utils packages or conftest.py files. The loader runs when the file is imported. It reportedly gets its next step from blockchain transaction data. The activity has been linked to North Korea and may date back to February 2025.

summary: CISA added 10 vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, which means it has evidence they are being exploited. Five affect Mitel MiCollab, including an arbitrary file upload flaw (CVE-2026-133275). The rest affect Juniper, Vates and Danfoss products. summary: SecurityWeek reports that CVE-2026-103406 in Juniper Session Smart Conductor is being exploited in attacks. Remote attackers can use the flaw to run arbitrary commands as root. The report does not give details on victims or how widely the flaw is being exploited.

headline: US Treasury's FinCEN investigates intrusion, takes systems offline and extends filing deadlines
summary: FinCEN, the US Treasury's financial intelligence unit, is investigating unauthorized access to a limited subset of its systems. It has taken some systems offline and extended reporting deadlines for financial institutions. The agency holds suspicious activity reports and other Bank Secrecy Act filings.

headline: Gap in earlier Drupal installer patch exploited for site takeover
summary: Drupal warns that its previous installer patch left some websites open to takeover. Attackers are already exploiting the gap. No CVE is cited in the source.

headline: 1Password says customer data was stolen through a compromised employee GitHub account
summary: 1Password disclosed that attackers hijacked an employee's corporate GitHub account and used it to deploy malicious code to backend services, which stole customer data. The full scope of the stolen data was not set out in the source summary.

headline: Attackers chain PHP2Shell and Fragnesia flaws against internet-exposed PAN-OS management interfaces
summary: Palo Alto Networks warns that threat actors are chaining the PHP2Shell and Fragnesia vulnerabilities to attack PAN-OS devices whose management interfaces are exposed to the internet. The source gives no CVE identifiers, victim counts or attribution.

headline: 13 malicious NuGet packages target .NET developers through fake job assessments
summary: Socket researchers found 13 malicious NuGet packages aimed at Windows .NET developers. The packages were offered as a fake take-home job assessment. Most pose as WinUI 3 and WPF button controls, and the analysed versions deliver malware when a developer builds or runs the project.
overrides: Global deployment applicability: every region 95%; cross-industry relevance at least 60%

headline: Drupal warns of exploitation of new highly critical CMS vulnerability
summary: The Drupal project is warning that attackers are exploiting a new vulnerability in the content management system that it rates highly critical. The report gives no CVE identifier or technical details.
overrides: No source-reported exploitation or recent KEV evidence; vulnerability capped at high

headline: 1Password breach via compromised employee GitHub account exposes customer data and internal source code
summary: An attacker used a compromised 1Password employee GitHub account to push malicious code, steal customer records and expose internal source code. 1Password says customer vaults were not accessed. The excerpt does not say how far the malicious code spread or which records were taken.

headline: CISA reports five Mitel MiCollab vulnerabilities exploited in attacks
summary: CISA reports that attackers are exploiting five vulnerabilities in the Mitel MiCollab VoIP and collaboration platform. The source summary does not list the CVE identifiers.
overrides: No source-reported exploitation or recent KEV evidence; vulnerability capped at high

headline: Mitel MiCollab zero-days exploited before advisory in suspected AI-assisted extortion campaign
summary: Accenture reports that attackers exploited Mitel MiCollab vulnerabilities before Mitel published its advisory, apparently as part of an extortion campaign. Researchers believe AI likely helped the attackers, but that is an assessment rather than a confirmed fact. The source summary names no CVE identifiers or victims.
overrides: No source-reported exploitation or recent KEV evidence; vulnerability capped at high

headline: CISA issues alert on critical flaw in Danfoss refrigeration controllers
summary: Danfoss has disclosed a critical flaw in its refrigeration controllers, and CISA has issued an alert about it. According to the report, food retailers are the main users of the affected equipment. The sources do not report any exploitation.

headline: CISA warns of critical unpatched flaw in Danfoss AK-SM 8xxA refrigeration controllers
summary: CISA has warned of a critical vulnerability in Danfoss AK-SM 8xxA Series controllers. Food retailers use these controllers to manage refrigeration, HVAC and lighting. Reports describe the flaw as unpatched, and the summary does not mention any active exploitation.

headline: Critical vulnerability in Copeland refrigeration systems exploited in attacks
summary: Attackers are reported to be exploiting a critical vulnerability in Copeland refrigeration systems. The source summary is cut off, so the exact impact, the affected models and any CVE identifier are not confirmed.

headline: Microsoft says Salt Typhoon and North Korean groups are adopting the Artex AI tool
summary: Microsoft reports that Artex, an AI tool linked to several high-profile breaches, is quickly being added to the toolkits of Chinese and North Korean hacking groups, including Salt Typhoon. The source summary gives no technical indicators.

headline: 1Password discloses backend breach via GitHub account; some customer data and source code accessed
summary: 1Password disclosed that an attacker got into some of its backend systems and accessed limited customer information. The headline reports that source code was stolen through a GitHub account compromise. The company says customer password vaults and other secrets were not accessed.

headline: 1Password reports backend breach via compromised employee GitHub account; vaults reportedly unaffected
summary: An attacker reportedly used a 1Password employee's hijacked GitHub account to reach backend systems and take customer data. According to the report, customer password vaults were not accessed. The scope of the exposed data and how the account was compromised are not detailed in the source.

headline: 1Password breached via hijacked employee GitHub account; customer names and emails copied
summary: An attacker took over a 1Password employee's corporate GitHub account. From there they copied some customer account records, including names and emails, and source code from private repositories. 1Password began investigating on November 19, 2026, and says it will keep updating its disclosure.

headline: 1Password breach exposes user data and source code
summary: Attackers got into 1Password systems and obtained personal data of some users along with source code. This Dutch-language report gives few details.

headline: US DOJ anti-scam surge charges over 800 defendants as FBI targets 29 scam compounds
summary: The US Justice Department reports that its anti-scam surge has targeted more than 800 defendants. The FBI says it has acted against more than 29 scam compounds. The summary gives no further detail on where the compounds are or what types of fraud were involved.

headline: Swiss and Italian agencies warn of autonomous AI-agent attacks on critical infrastructure
summary: Cybersecurity agencies in Switzerland and Italy have warned that automated attacks driven by AI agents are targeting critical infrastructure organisations. The source summary does not name specific victims, techniques or vulnerabilities.

headline: Google to require MCP or CLI access for Workspace AI agents from February 2027
summary: Google announced security controls for AI agents in Workspace and Google Cloud. They include dedicated agent identities, human approval for sensitive operations, prompt-injection screening and limits on third-party AI tool access. Workspace MCP servers and the CLI are now generally available, and agent access through them becomes mandatory from February 2027.
watch_tech: Google Cloud; Model Context Protocol (MCP); AI agent frameworks

headline: Google Cloud to require approved MCP or CLI methods for AI agent access to Workspace
summary: Google Cloud will soon require AI agents to connect to Gmail, Drive and Docs through Workspace MCP servers or its command-line interface. The change affects organisations whose agent integrations use other access methods. No effective date was given.

headline: UK delays National Cyber Action Plan publication to December 9
summary: The UK government has delayed its National Cyber Action Plan, which it had planned to publish in mid-November. Officials now aim to release the strategy for defending the wider economy against state-backed and criminal hackers on December 9.

headline: Microsoft says multiple state-linked actors abuse the ARTEX agentic AI pentest framework
summary: Microsoft reports that several threat actors, including state-linked groups, have abused ARTEX, an AI-powered penetration testing framework. Named groups include Onyx Sleet, Pearl Sleet and Salt Typhoon. According to Microsoft, the tool helps them speed up existing reconnaissance, credential attacks and web application exploitation.

headline: Incomplete fix in moby/sys/user lets crafted passwd/group files cause denial of service
summary: The earlier fix for CVE-2026-61801 did not apply file size limits to several parsing and lookup functions in github.com/moby/sys/user. A malicious /etc/passwd or /etc/group file, for example inside a container image, could exhaust memory or CPU. The issue is fixed in v0.5.1 and Docker Engine 29.10.1, and impact depends on how each application uses these functions.

headline: UK ICO reprimands Home Office over data integrity failings at the border
summary: The UK Information Commissioner's Office has reprimanded the Home Office over data integrity failings that caused distress to people at the border. The action falls under UK data protection law.

headline: Vendor research ranks phishing kits by how often they get past email and web controls
summary: Push Security published research that measures a "breakthrough rate": how often attacks from each phishing kit get past email security, web gateways and safe browsing to reach users. It identifies which kits and techniques most often evade these layered controls.

headline: Keycloak flaw may accept password-only SSO sessions where OTP is required
summary: When a Keycloak client policy requires an OTP-based high-assurance flow, keycloak-services may wrongly accept an existing password-only SSO session. An attacker with a user's password or session could skip the second factor and obtain tokens claiming higher assurance. No exploitation is reported.

headline: Netherlands considers national DNS-based phishing filter enabled by default
summary: The Netherlands may introduce a DNS-based phishing filter that would be switched on by default for everyone. The source describes this as a possibility, not a decision, and gives no implementation details.

headline: Florida ransomware recovery firm CEO indicted over alleged hidden ransom payments to hackers
summary: A federal grand jury has indicted the CEO of a ransomware recovery firm. He is accused of misrepresenting the firm's services and secretly paying ransoms to cybercriminals. These are allegations only, and the case has not been decided.

headline: librelp TLS flaw with GnuTLS driver skips peer certificate chain verification
summary: CVE-2026-132888 affects librelp when it is configured for TLS certificate validation with the GnuTLS driver. The library does not verify the peer certificate chain. A remote attacker could present an invalid or self-signed certificate and act as a trusted log source or collector. The Amazon Linux record does not confirm whether Amazon Linux is affected or whether a patch exists.

headline: FortiGuard finds over 4,400 malicious holiday-shopping domains ahead of the season
summary: FortiGuard Labs found more than 24,000 newly registered shopping-themed domains over 90 days and classified over 4,400 of them as malicious. The report expects retailer impersonation, payment fraud and account takeover this holiday season. It also notes that underground markets trade stolen customer data and access to e-commerce systems.

headline: Microsoft says Chinese and North Korean state actors have adopted the ARTEX AI offensive framework
summary: Microsoft has confirmed that nation-state actors are using the ARTEX AI offensive framework in their tooling; the headline attributes this to Chinese and North Korean groups. The CSA describes the tool as part of a "third wave" of AI-driven threats.

headline: Remus infostealer uses fake Google Sheets Chrome extension to steal Gmail messages
summary: The Remus infostealer uses a malicious Chrome extension that poses as Google Sheets to steal Gmail messages. Its operators advertised this as a Gmail zero-day, but the report describes it as extension abuse rather than a flaw in Gmail.

headline: Amazon Linux lists CVE-2026-135901 security fix for shadow newgidmap
summary: Amazon Linux Security Center published a CVE record for a security fix to newgidmap in the shadow package. The record does not establish which Amazon Linux versions are affected or whether patches are available, and no severity or exploitation details are provided.

headline: Newly identified Iranian group Volant Manticore is spying on organisations in Cyprus
summary: Researchers describe a previously undocumented Iranian threat group, Volant Manticore, that is targeting organisations in Cyprus to gather intelligence. The excerpt does not name targeted sectors or give technical details.

headline: QEMU-KVM flaw could let a privileged guest read host QEMU process memory
summary: A flaw in qemu-kvm, reported for Red Hat Enterprise Linux, could let a privileged user inside a guest VM copy parts of host QEMU process memory into guest memory. This could expose sensitive information that helps further attacks. The record notes no exploitation and does not confirm Amazon Linux status.

headline: SYS01 infostealer variant abuses browser management to force an email-stealing extension
summary: A new version of the SYS01 infostealer is spreading through Meta ads. It enrolls victims' browsers into enterprise-style management so it can force-install an extension that steals data, including Gmail and Outlook email.

headline: Phishers abuse Hugging Face Spaces AI site builder to spoof major brands
summary: Aikido found 42 phishing pages hosted on Hugging Face Spaces that impersonate major brands. About two-thirds of the pages were built with the platform's AI site builder.

headline: Linux kernel Bluetooth L2CAP fix rejects invalid TxWindow in configuration requests (CVE-2026-99807)
summary: A Linux kernel flaw in Bluetooth L2CAP handling has been fixed: the kernel now rejects invalid TxWindow values in configuration requests. The record gives no severity, exploitation status or Amazon Linux affected or patch status. Any attack would most likely need to come from within Bluetooth range.

headline: MongoDB Python driver TLS revocation check flaw may accept revoked certificates
summary: CVE-2026-135146 affects the optional TLS revocation-checking support in the MongoDB Python driver. An endpoint operator holding a revoked but unexpired certificate that the client trusts could have the connection accepted. This could expose credentials and session data. Exploitation requires control of the endpoint the client connects to.

headline: rsyslog omdtls name and fingerprint modes fail to verify DTLS server identity (CVE-2026-132145)
summary: In the omdtls output module, the name and fingerprint authentication modes reportedly do not verify the DTLS server's identity. This could let an attacker in a network position intercept or redirect forwarded logs. No severity or exploitation details were given, and Amazon Linux affected status is not established.

headline: Australia passes Digital Duty of Care Act requiring online providers to prevent foreseeable harms
summary: Australia's Parliament has passed the Digital Duty of Care Act. The law requires online providers to set up protocols that protect users from serious harms, including threats of violence. The source does not state an effective date.

headline: US indicts data recovery firm co-founder for allegedly secretly paying ransomware gangs
summary: A co-founder of a Florida data recovery firm has been charged in Rhode Island with three counts of wire fraud. Prosecutors allege he secretly paid ransomware gangs while telling victims his company did not. He was arrested in Las Vegas on October 22.

headline: CVE-2026-40558: Perl Net::FTP flaw lets malicious FTP servers redirect passive-mode data connections
summary: A flaw in Perl's libnet Net::FTP module lets a malicious FTP server redirect a client's passive-mode data connection to an arbitrary third-party host. Net::FTP ships with Perl, and libnet v3.17 includes a fix. Amazon Linux's record does not confirm whether Amazon Linux is affected or whether a patch is available.

headline: Linux kernel Bluetooth L2CAP fix uses default TxWindow when socket option is zero (CVE-2026-99808)
summary: A Linux kernel fix makes Bluetooth L2CAP fall back to the default TxWindow when a socket option sets it to zero. The record gives no severity, exploitation status or Amazon Linux patch status.

headline: Linux kernel vfio/cdx flaw could let read-only region mappings become writable
summary: A fixed Linux kernel bug in the vfio/cdx driver could allow read-only device region mappings to become writable. The record gives no severity, exploitation status or confirmation of which Amazon Linux versions are affected.

headline: Flatpak portal flaw CVE-2026-133845 could expose file descriptors to a subsandbox
summary: An unprivileged Flatpak app could trick flatpak-portal into giving a subsandbox access to one of the app's own file descriptors. The CVE record does not confirm whether Amazon Linux is affected or whether a patch is available. No exploitation is reported.

headline: Flatpak system-helper privilege escalation flaw CVE-2026-133842 disclosed
summary: The flatpak-system-helper extra-data handling could allow privilege escalation when canonicalizing permissions fails with an EMFILE error, meaning the process has run out of file descriptors. The CVE record does not confirm whether Amazon Linux is affected or patched. No exploitation is reported.

headline: FIFA discloses breach exposing a limited set of personal and business information
summary: FIFA, the Switzerland-based governing body for football, says hackers accessed a limited set of personal and business information. It is working with authorities and law enforcement, and the scope and attack method have not been disclosed.

headline: Kaspersky finds preinstalled Keenadu firmware malware on more than 220,000 Android devices
summary: Kaspersky reports that Keenadu firmware malware was preinstalled on more than 220,000 Android devices in the first ten months of 2026. Together with the older Triada family, it accounts for most preinstalled-malware detections. Kaspersky says monthly detections of such devices have grown more than 2.5 times over the past year.

headline: CVE-2026-44842 addresses parser resource exhaustion through unlimited nesting depth
summary: The CVE record describes a parser fix that limits nesting depth by default, because deep nesting grows stack use and processing work. The record does not name the affected component or confirm Amazon Linux affected status or patch availability.

headline: French hospital suspends cancer treatments after cyberattack
summary: A hospital in France has temporarily stopped cancer treatments following a cyberattack. The source excerpt does not name the attackers or say what type of attack it was.

headline: Socket CEO discusses fixing open-source vulnerabilities without upgrading dependencies
summary: Socket CEO Feross Aboukhadijeh appeared on the Risky Business podcast to discuss fixing open-source vulnerabilities at scale without upgrading dependencies. The piece is vendor commentary and reports no new vulnerability or incident.

headline: CBS: AI use by Dutch businesses more than doubles in a year
summary: Statistics Netherlands (CBS) reports that AI use by Dutch companies more than doubled within one year.

headline: Dutch Ministry of Economic Affairs funds resilient digital time infrastructure with €250,000
summary: The Dutch Ministry of Economic Affairs is putting €250,000 toward developing a resilient digital time service. The source gives few details about scope or timeline.

headline: Linux kernel Bluetooth L2CAP fix rejects mode changes on connected channels
summary: CVE-2026-99806 fixes a Linux kernel Bluetooth L2CAP issue so that mode changes on already-connected channels are rejected. The record gives no detail on impact or severity. Exposure is limited to systems with Bluetooth enabled.

headline: Dutch MPs question education state secretary on Google Search AI Mode's impact on pupils
summary: Members of the Dutch parliament have asked the education state secretary about how Google Search's AI Mode affects primary school pupils. The questions are a policy inquiry and do not involve a security incident.

headline: Linux kernel vfio/fsl-mc fix stops read-only region mappings from becoming writable
summary: CVE-2026-99810 fixes a Linux kernel vfio/fsl-mc issue where read-only region mappings could become writable. The driver is specific to NXP Freescale Management Complex platforms, which limits exposure. No severity score or exploitation is reported.

headline: GIMP GIF loader integer overflow may enable heap overflow via crafted JIF file
summary: CVE-2026-136329 is a 32-bit integer overflow in GIMP's file-gif-load plugin. A crafted JIF file causes an undersized heap allocation, which can crash the application and may allow code execution. Exploitation requires a user to open a malicious file.

headline: Gartner again names Microsoft a Leader in its 2026 SIEM Magic Quadrant
summary: Microsoft says Gartner has again named it a Leader in the 2026 Magic Quadrant for SIEM. The source is a vendor marketing announcement.

headline: Incogni survey: most US adults would pay to remove personal data from search results
summary: Incogni surveyed 1,008 US adults about online privacy. 55% said they would pay to have their personal information permanently removed from public search results. 53% said they would like a log of who searched their name, covering the past five years.

headline: Commentary: social media age limits alone will not make platforms safer
summary: More countries are introducing age limits and age verification for social media and other platforms. This opinion piece argues that such limits do not make platforms safer and do not solve the underlying problem.

headline: Proxmox VE 9.3 adds production-supported snapshots for SAN-backed VMs
summary: Proxmox Virtual Environment 9.3 adds production support for snapshots on shared LVM storage over iSCSI and Fibre Channel SANs. Each guest also gets an identity that persists across migration, backup and restore.

headline: Anthropic describes migrating its Messages API backend from Python to Rust
summary: Anthropic published an engineering write-up on moving its Messages API from Python to Rust. The source does not describe a vulnerability, incident or security event.

headline: SQLite's sqlite3_rsync tool enables remote database snapshots without a full local copy
summary: A blog post covers sqlite3_rsync, a SQLite utility that copies or synchronises a database over SSH by exchanging page hashes. It can take a snapshot without first needing enough local disk space for a duplicate copy. The post is about operations and backups, and it reports no security issue.

headline: Essay quote criticises homogenised AI-generated content
summary: A blog post quotes an essay arguing that AI-generated text from Claude is making videos, talks and email pitches sound alike. It is commentary and contains no security incident or vulnerability.

headline: Scott Aaronson comments on AI's impact on mathematical discovery
summary: Simon Willison quotes Scott Aaronson saying that AI is opening up large new areas of mathematical and complexity-theory results. The piece has no security content.

headline: Datasette-charts plugin released with automatic chart suggestions and Datasette Agent integration
summary: The new datasette-charts plugin suggests and builds charts from full query results using aggregating SQL, and it saves chart state in the URL fragment. Version 0.2a0 lets Datasette Agent create charts from chat requests. These are alpha feature releases with no security content.

headline: Blogger comments on newspaper photojournalism editing standards amid Photoshop AI feature concerns
summary: A blog post shares a Hacker News comment about a newspaper's strict rules against editing news photos. It was posted in a discussion about AI features in Photoshop. It has no security content.

headline: Roundup of Black Friday 2026 discounts on security products
summary: Help Net Security published a list of Black Friday discounts on security tools, including a self-hosted password manager. The article is promotional and reports no threat.

headline: Socket releases free syntax highlighting theme for VS Code, Vim and Neovim
summary: Socket has released Socket Calm, a free open-source syntax highlighting theme for code editors. The release has no security implications.

headline: Cisco Talos publishes Thanksgiving opinion piece thanking security community
summary: Cisco Talos published a seasonal opinion column that thanks the cybersecurity community and criticises threat actors. It reports no new threat, vulnerability or incident.
